status: design only; not implemented or submitted
objective: Locate first numerical divergence between original and matrix-layout default QDWH before proposing another optimization.
hypotheses: Small Gram differences may be amplified by regularized spectral powers or later operations.
Sharding changes may alter eigensolver results or compiler/reduction choices outside the eigensolver.
Polar iteration may amplify differences; similar direction errors alone do not identify the cause.

controls.geometry: Full original 11-layer matrices, no blocks or approximation
controls.storage: synthetic regional data only, no cross-region checkpoint read

sequence: Generate the identical original synthetic state and gradients and compute one common refreshed state. Compare its fingerprint and all leaves before branching.

Feed the same frozen Grams into original and matrix-layout power functions. Compare normalized Grams, eigenvalue ranges, eigenpair residuals, orthogonality and reconstructed powers; do not compare raw eigenvectors elementwise because signs and degenerate bases vary.
Feed each power pair plus identical momentum into one common reconstruction/inner-product function. Compare inner matrices, polar outputs and final directions.
Cross-feed identical powers/inner matrices into the original and candidate downstream layouts to separate solver differences from downstream compiler/reduction effects.
Compare staged results against fused full updates on identical inputs. Stage barriers are diagnostic instrumentation, not evidence of an accepted optimization.
operational_requirements: Implement and validate CPU harness with online W&B before any accelerator submission.
Publish exact source and plan before one sequential diagnostic. Preserve default preemption retries and no wall-clock limits.
Stream per-stage summaries and offload comparison arrays to host outside timings; free unused device buffers and caches.
No training promotion without unchanged numerical gate, saved-state regional validation, full restoration and measured training MFU.
